Start a Reproducibility Bundle Project

Source: R/mkbndl.R
mkbndlproj.Rd

Writes a starter project that mkbndl() packs as it is: a config.json with the project's details, a data_provenance.json to pin the data file and describe synthetic data, and an analysis.R that reads the data, records its checks with recrd() and writes manifest.json. Edit the three files for the real project; the starter runs from the first build, on synthetic data, so every step can be tried before the analysis is written.

Usage

mkbndlproj(
  dir,
  name = basename(dir),
  title = name,
  author = "",
  contact = "",
  overwrite = FALSE
)

Arguments

dir

Folder for the project, created if needed.

name

Short project name used in the zip's name, default the folder's name.

title

Title shown in the bundle's pages, default name.

author, contact

Who the reviewer contacts; default empty.

overwrite

Replace starter files that exist, default FALSE.

Value

An object of class rmbl_bundle_project: a list with dir and files (the files written). It prints as a box.

Details

The starter's data is a CSV with columns group and value; its one check is the row count, so the first run on synthetic data shows one INFO. Set resource$filename, resource$direct_url and resource$sha256 in data_provenance.json (see sha256file()) and the runner finds, downloads and checks the real file.

Errors: dir holding any of the three files when overwrite is FALSE; a name with characters other than letters, digits, dot, dash and underscore.

See also

mkbndl() to build the bundle.

Examples

p <- mkbndlproj(file.path(tempdir(), "my-study"), title = "My study")
p
#> ╭── Bundle project ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
#> │   Folder  /tmp/RtmpAwgnfi/my-study                                          │
#> │   Files   config.json, data_provenance.json, analysis.R                     │
#> │                                                                             │
#> │   Edit config.json (who and what), data_provenance.json (the data file,     │
#> │   its URL and SHA-256) and analysis.R (the checks), then build the zip      │
#> │   with mkbndl().                                                            │
#> │   It runs as it is on synthetic data, so the bundle can be tried before     │
#> │   the analysis is written.                                                  │
#> ╰─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
readLines(file.path(p$dir, "analysis.R"), n = 5)
#> [1] "## analysis.R -- the analysis of this bundle. The runner (setup_and_run.R)"
#> [2] "## calls it as:  Rscript analysis.R <data file> <results folder>"          
#> [3] "## with BRICKLAYER_SYNTHETIC=1 set when the data are synthetic. It writes" 
#> [4] "## manifest.json into the results folder: one record per check, with the"  
#> [5] "## value the paper reports and the value this run computed."               

# files are kept unless overwrite = TRUE
try(mkbndlproj(p$dir))
#> Error : /tmp/RtmpAwgnfi/my-study already holds config.json, data_provenance.json, analysis.R: pass overwrite = TRUE to replace
